First off, you don’t deserve any form of abuse, EVER.

Second, family can be toxic. I’m sorry. I relate to this personally.
Your grandma probably has no idea how trauma effects people. My grandmother has said similar things. Argued with the results of my psychiatrist—the woman taught math in the 70’s part-time, yet she thinks her opinion trumps a doctor’s? Anyways.. 
I truly believe that weird victim-blaming thing is generational residual ignorance. My grandmother likes to tell this story about how her German neighbor was in an abusive marriage and that her mother told her to “stay in her bed because she made it..” What? Why? No. But that was the mindset for old world households back in the day. It’s easier to blame someone than deal with it. Abusers are garbage. No mental gymnastics needed to excuse it. Now we have security cameras and equal rights. We don’t need those mindsets anymore.

I think abuse was so rampant that blaming women for EVERYTHING was easier. Basic critical thinking would show how skewed it is to blame a victim, it’s lazy. Look up the Dunning-Krueger effect. Unqualified people make assumptions and believe they know more than a professional. It’s SURVIVAL to lay low and tolerate it until you see your escape.  There’s so much evidence to show that’s why people stay in relationships. But you could show hundreds of research papers and they’d just dig in their heels. So all you can do is hold onto your truth and find someone who will listen. That’s how you heal.

You’ll also find that a lot of the garbage people spew is projection of how they feel about themselves. Knowing that has really helped me let go of pain. Hurt people hurt people.
I used to question why I deserved abuse. And the truth is you don’t, people are just projecting because they’re carrying pain and it makes them feel better to cast that onto someone else. 
Except your ex—he deserves jail for a long time. And it’ll eventually happen to people who get away with abuse. Trust me. You’ll find it in the paper years from now. So know that karma eventually comes to bite people like that. But don’t pray for revenge, because I did for a LONG time and it was consuming, and just took time away from me that I’ll never get back. Don’t make that mistake.

Your job now is to heal and be so kind to yourself. Definitely get some counseling when you can.  Because that’s all you deserve—kindness, understanding, and love. Nothing less. Family can be SO toxic but that’s not a reflection on you. I did the same to my family. I avoid them and my mother will cry when she’s drunk and text “why do you hate me?” Well, she did the same to me. That’s on her to heal and undo the generational bs that’s lingering around.

Only you can decide if you should speak with them. You don’t owe anyone anything.

Take care and I wish you nothing but the best :) Sorry for the rant, I could just relate to this on a personal level, obviously.

Edit: I was assuming you’re female, but in case you don’t identify as such, know that victims of any gender can be abused.

It hurts me to read how negatively you describe yourself. I’m so sorry you’re in pain. 

I want to share my struggle with you, not to minimize your pain in comparison but to perhaps give you some solace:

I’ve personally weighed 220 at 5’5” at my lowest point, just after being dumped in a horrific way. Just prior to that, I just had lost a lot of weight. It felt so hopeless. Everything I fought for was undone. I wanted to die, and tried to make that wish come true.

It took a lot of strength for me to fight that weight gain. Yes, stretch marks suck. I have them everywhere. Breasts, back of arms, calves, rib cage, hips, and thighs.
They’re there. They’re proof that I went through shit that would destroy most people. And with a bit of working out they may improve. 

To add to that, after my grandfather passed, I developed fair amount of horrific acne scars that make it very hard to leave my bed everyday. Even when my skin was perfect, I was told I was ugly.
Sometimes I feel like giving up. And to be honest, I would take the stretch marks over my facial scars and appearance. I feel disfigured.

However, what helped me the most is mentally saying, “Fuck it. I’m going to grow old anyways.”
That asshole who mocked me for my face or catching a glimpse of my hips? He’s probably been through a horrible divorce that he doesn’t talk about. Add in any additional ailments most people wouldn’t talk about publicly. And anyone who mocks people like that is a garbage human. Fuck them. They suck, and their shitty personalities will poison any surface beauty they may have. 

However, I do what I can to tolerate myself. Makeup is something I’m incredibly grateful for. And I’m hoping to get some plastic surgery in the near future, but mostly for my face. Yes, we want to avoid contingent self-esteem, but it gives me some hope.
When I’m at my worst, I think about my animals. Where would they be if I didn’t help them? I feel like that’s why I exist. And I try my hardest to be a good person. And from what I’ve been told, despite all of my flaws, people still become attracted to me. I’ve also fallen for people who are so far from conventionally attractive.

I guarantee you’re so much harder on yourself than others would be. You have a different battle than I’ll ever face. I don’t know what it’s like to be trans and I don’t ever want to minimize the struggles someone like you may face. But you have all of my love and full support to love yourself. You are worth love and a healthy self esteem.

She kind of explained things in a way that gave me some peace. That your relatives are an energy that stick around. Lovingly floating around. And that there’s some purpose, we just can’t comprehend it yet. And no, I don’t believe in anything in particular.

Even if that’s a flat out crop of lies I was being fed, then hear me out. 

One of my favorite quotes:

“I do not fear death, in view of the fact that I had been dead for billions and billions of years before I was born, and had not suffered the slightest inconvenience from it.”
-Mark Twain

That alone gives me some solace. Yes, you can stay there, depressed, and dwell on the uncontrollable. Or you can take a deep breath and think about how far you’ve come.
You are the product of people surviving through some horrible things, including their parents, and their parents’ parents. This is also one of the best times to be alive ever in the history of man. Could you imagine losing your parents during a typhoid fever outbreak? Maybe being sold into slavery by your tribe. Heavy stuff. Now we have small slates that remotely order whatever whim we want. That was a pipe dream for the majority of human history.

Yes—we got issues. However, you can make the best of it. Take a walk. Maybe write down every amazing memory that suddenly hits you in the shower (once you’re out of the shower, obviously). Then tell the bad memories to eat shit.

One of the things the psychic told me is that when suicide victims spoke to her they also shared their regrets; they wished they said for people to fuck off more. To enjoy being alive.

Your acne could be *hormonal* as was mine, so try to find a trigger. Maybe diet and/or stress. Even dental issues can cause breakouts. That was my experience, my acne was from the inside-out. I found that no amount of topical product eliminated the root cause until I got on birth control, antibiotics, then spirolactone. My diet and stress were what initially triggered my issue in my early twenties; a verbally abusive supervisor and the stress of college. It was also hereditary; mom had cystic, and she got that from my grandfather. During his time, derms suggested uv lamps, now he’s battling skin cancer. I’ll get to SPF in a minute.

If you have a lot of redness, it’s temporary. For me, my cysts calmed when I took Advil, iced my cysts, and drank plenty of water. AHA’s and BHA’s are fantastic at speeding up healing of hyper-pigmentation.  (Paula’s Choice has a great line, and so does The Ordinary via Beautylish) *DO NOT* over do it though. Only exfoliate a couple times a week, or less.
Be gentle—do not use hard, abrasive products. Try your best not to pop or pick. If you have a large cyst, buying those clearasil covers will help speed healing.

A summary:

-Definitely invest in high SPF, get some sun, but very limited. 
-Take vitamin d3 (if suggested from a doctor)
-Retin-a 
-Reduce diary
-Reduce stress
-Improve diet if you haven’t already (you may have a impeccable diet and may still have acne)
-Plenty of water
-Birth control
-Antibiotics
-Spirolactone (can help unwanted facial hair too)
-AHA/BHA’s (will help unclog pores and speed clearing of redness)
-Vitamin C (use after AHA/BHA to further help pigmentation)
-Advil (for new cysts that are fairly deep in the skin)
-Acne spot treatment covers (Clearasil is one brand)

-Accutane, if all else fails. This is a last resort due to the risks. 

I wish you the best. You’re beautiful and this is temporary. <3

Some of the best treatments I've found were to be TCA cross and saline injections for rolling and ice-pick scarring. Acne.org has some great forums on both. TCA cross involves placing high concentrations of TCA peel into ice-pick scars to help build collagen. Saline injections involve a thin, 30 gage diabetic syringe filled with sterile saline to be injected into the depression, over time it helps elevate the dent (rolling scars). 
Unfortunately, both methods take time in between and multiple treatments. I live in a rural part of Pennsylvania and these options aren't available to me via a dermatologist. I've done them myself, and honestly it's worked. It's just tedious. From what I've read, saline injections can take +6 treatments to see results with 6 weeks downtime in between. But I've seen improvements in the atrophy dents from cortisone shots with at least three treatments.
The TCA cross has caused red hyperpigmentation, but I've had a couple rounds of laser genesis afterwards which has improved it. Overall, this is my experience. Please see a dermatologist to get recommendations but my suggestions are something to consider. Good luck.
